baslik: The Missing Valve That Destroyed an Oil Platform

sahneler.metin: Explosions destroyed Piper Alpha after a safety valve went missing.
The fire spread; of two hundred twenty six aboard, one hundred sixty five died.
A pressure safety valve had been removed for maintenance.
Its pipe was sealed only with a temporary cover.
The next shift did not know, and restarted the pump.
Pipelines from other platforms kept feeding the fire.
Offshore operators then had to prove their safety cases.

aciklama:
Piper Alpha was destroyed by explosions and fire in the North Sea. The cause: condensate leaking from a temporary blank flange, igniting, then oil and gas fires fed by connected pipelines.

kanitlar.iddia: At the time of the disaster, 226 people were on the platform; 165 died and 61 survived.
kanitlar.alinti: At the time of the disaster, 226 people were on the platform; 165 died and 61 survived.

kanitlar.iddia: A pressure safety valve had been removed from the pump for routine maintenance.
kanitlar.alinti: Two permits were issued to that effect, one for a pump overhaul and another for the removal of the pump's pressure safety valve (PSV #504), which was due for recertification.
Before anyone could act, the gas ignited and exploded.

kanitlar.iddia: Pipelines from other platforms continued to feed oil and gas to the fire.
kanitlar.alinti: Like many other offshore platforms, Piper Alpha had an automatic fire-fighting system, driven by both diesel and electric fire pumps.

kanitlar.iddia: The disaster led to safety cases for offshore installations.
kanitlar.alinti: The recommendations led to the enactment of the Offshore Safety Act 1992 and the making of the Offshore Installations (Safety Case) Regulations 1992.
